page: Amazon Web Services m7g.large is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the ARMv8 64-bit architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical CPU cores using AWS Neoverse-V1 processors clocked at 2.6 GHz, running one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. It is configured with 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache. It operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, has no integrated local storage, and includes no GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluation shows average single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-core capacity due to the 2-core boundary. In single-core testing, the instance achieved a stress-ng score of 1532.88 and a Geekbench score of 1444.0, both placing within the middle 50% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 24.19 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression scored 9.0 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics rank in the lower brackets, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 3040.69 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 2596.0. Memory bandwidth measured 53.4 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 20.78 GB/sec for uncached write blocks. In application benchmarks, the server achieved 3.2 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 4.09 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

With its 1:4 resource ratio and dedicated physical Arm cores, the m7g.large provides an efficient footprint for workloads with predictable, moderate resource requirements. Because it features no bundled local disks, external block storage is required for persistent data. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, mid-tier application hosting, continuous integration runners, and small-scale caching layers.
description: Amazon Web Services m7g.large is a general-purpose Nitro instance powered by the 64-bit arm64 architecture with 2 dedicated AWS Neoverse-V1 cores running at 2.6 GHz. It offers 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no integrated local NVMe storage and no GPU hardware. Synthetic benchmarks place its single-core compute performance in the average tier, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1444.0 and gzip compression of 24.19 GB/sec, while multi-core throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit. Real-world throughput reaches 3.2 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.09 GB/sec in static web delivery. The m7g.large is engineered for containerized microservices, development environments, CI/CD tasks, and low-to-moderate web traffic.
